raw_response:
I will keep the same wheat-maize rotation on all 4.1 mu, because on a small holding like mine I do not split land unless there is a strong price reason. I farm from what worked on my field before, then I adjust a little for water, fertilizer price, and yield target. Since I have well irrigation, I will push wheat a bit harder than a dryland farmer, because wheat here pays back if I keep the stand even and do not let it suffer at jointing and grain filling. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, plough or deep-rotate after maize straw, put most phosphorus and potassium in the base, and split nitrogen so I do not waste too much early but still protect yield. For maize, I will use a hybrid, sow right after wheat harvest, and keep the field clean and uniform. I would rather spend a little extra on nitrogen than lose ears and grain weight, but on 4.1 mu I still count every bag, so I will not go to demonstration-field levels. I will aim for solid, dependable yield, not record yield. I will keep pesticide use to what is needed for rust, aphid, armyworm, and leaf disease pressure, and I will rely on my well for the key water timings rather than waiting on rain.
